statements.matter: Matter is anything that occupies space and has mass. A gas is as much matter as a solid is, even though you can neither see nor hold it.
statements.density: The density of a substance is the ratio of the mass of a sample to its volume. It is an intensive property, so it identifies a substance rather than a sample: a brick of gold and a brick of lead of the same size do not have the same mass.

new.name: Chemistry
new.statement: Chemistry is the study of the composition, properties, and interactions of matter.

new.name: Hypothesis
new.statement: A hypothesis is a tentative explanation of observations that acts as a guide for gathering and checking information.

new.name: Law
new.statement: A law is a statement that summarizes a vast number of experimental observations and describes or predicts some aspect of the natural world.

new.name: Theory
new.statement: A theory is a well-substantiated, comprehensive, testable explanation of a particular aspect of nature.

new.name: Mass, $m$
new.statement: The mass of an object is a measure of the amount of matter in it, and it does not change with where the object is.

new.name: Weight
new.statement: The weight of an object is the force that gravity exerts on it, so it changes with the gravity the object is in.

new.name: Unit
new.statement: A unit is a standard of comparison for measurements; the number of a measured quantity says how many of its unit the quantity holds.

new.name: Length
new.statement: Length is the measure of one dimension of an object, and its SI unit is the meter.

new.name: Time, $t$
new.statement: Time is measured in the SI base unit of time, the second.

new.name: Temperature, $T$
new.statement: Temperature is an intensive property representing the hotness or coldness of matter, and its SI unit is the kelvin.

new.name: Macroscopic domain
new.statement: The macroscopic domain is the realm of everyday things that are large enough to sense directly by human sight and touch.

new.name: Microscopic domain
new.statement: The microscopic domain is the realm of things that are much too small to be sensed directly.

new.name: Symbolic domain
new.statement: The symbolic domain is the specialized language used to represent components of the macroscopic and microscopic domains, such as chemical symbols, chemical formulas, chemical equations, graphs, drawings, and calculations.

new.name: Gas
new.statement: A gas is a state of matter that has neither definite volume nor shape.

new.name: Liquid
new.statement: A liquid is a state of matter that has a definite volume but indefinite shape.

new.name: Solid
new.statement: A solid is a state of matter that is rigid, has a definite shape, and has a fairly constant volume.

new.name: Plasma
new.statement: A plasma is a gaseous state of matter containing a large number of electrically charged atoms and/or molecules.

new.name: Pure substance
new.statement: A pure substance is a homogeneous substance that has a constant composition.

new.name: Element
new.statement: An element is a substance composed of a single type of atom, one that cannot be decomposed by a chemical change.

new.name: Compound
new.statement: A compound is a pure substance that can be decomposed into two or more elements.

new.name: Mixture
new.statement: A mixture is matter that can be separated into its components by physical means.

new.name: Heterogeneous mixture
new.statement: A heterogeneous mixture is a combination of substances with a composition that varies from point to point.

new.name: Homogeneous mixture
new.statement: A homogeneous mixture, also called a solution, is a combination of substances with a composition that is uniform throughout.

new.name: Atom
new.statement: An atom is the smallest particle of an element that can enter into a chemical combination.

new.name: Molecule
new.statement: A molecule is a bonded collection of two or more atoms of the same or different elements.

new.name: Physical change
new.statement: A physical change is a change in the state or properties of matter that does not involve a change in its chemical composition.

new.name: Chemical change
new.statement: A chemical change is a change producing a different kind of matter from the original kind of matter.

new.name: Extensive property
new.statement: An extensive property is a property of a substance that depends on the amount of the substance.

new.name: Intensive property
new.statement: An intensive property is a property of a substance that is independent of the amount of the substance.

new.name: SI units
new.statement: SI units are the standards fixed by international agreement in the International System of Units (Le Système International d’Unités).

new.name: Meter, m
new.statement: The meter (m) is the standard metric and SI unit of length; 1 m is approximately 1.094 yards.

new.name: Kilogram, kg
new.statement: The kilogram (kg) is the standard SI unit of mass.

new.name: Second, s
new.statement: The second (s) is the SI unit of time.

new.name: Kelvin, K
new.statement: The kelvin (K) is the SI unit of temperature; 273.15 K equals 0 °C.

new.name: Celsius, °C
new.statement: The degree Celsius (°C) is a unit of temperature; water freezes at 0 °C and boils at 100 °C on this scale.

new.name: Fahrenheit, °F
new.statement: The degree Fahrenheit (°F) is a unit of temperature; water freezes at 32 °F and boils at 212 °F on this scale.

new.name: Cubic meter, m³
new.statement: The cubic meter (m³) is the SI unit of volume, the volume of a cube with an edge length of exactly 1 m.

new.name: Cubic centimeter, cm³
new.statement: The cubic centimeter (cm³ or cc) is the volume of a cube with an edge length of exactly 1 cm.

new.name: Liter, L
new.statement: The liter (L), also called the cubic decimeter, is a unit of volume; 1 L equals 1,000 cm³.

new.name: Milliliter, mL
new.statement: The milliliter (mL) is 1/1,000 of a liter and equals 1 cm³.

new.name: Exact number
new.statement: An exact number is a number derived by counting or by definition.

new.name: Uncertainty
new.statement: The uncertainty of a measurement is an estimate of the amount by which it differs from the true value.

new.name: Rounding
new.statement: Rounding is the procedure used to ensure that calculated results properly reflect the uncertainty in the measurements used in the calculation.

new.name: Accuracy
new.statement: Accuracy is how closely a measurement aligns with a correct value.

new.name: Precision
new.statement: Precision is how closely a measurement matches the same measurement when repeated.
